transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I guess I'm here because I just can't seem to settle down. It's like I can't be comfortable in my own skin anymore. I just... I always feel like I have to jump up and do the next thing, even when I'm completely worn out and know I should just be sitting still. It's exhausting.
How long have you been experiencing this feeling of not being able to settle down and always needing to move on to the next thing?
Well... I suppose it's been really bad for a while now. Um... since my husband passed away. That was about... a year and ten months ago, I guess.
Besides this restlessness and feeling like you can't settle down, have you also been experiencing persistent sadness or a feeling of emptiness since your husband passed away?
No... not really. I mean, I miss him, of course. But... I don't think it's like that. I'm just... tired of always feeling so keyed up.
When you think back to right after your husband passed away, did this restless, keyed-up feeling start immediately, or did it develop gradually over weeks or months?
I don't really remember exactly. It's just... been there. I didn't keep track of when it started.

When you feel this keyed-up, restless feeling, is there usually something specific you're worried or anxious about, or does it feel more like a general sense of being on edge without a particular worry in mind?
No... I don't think I'm worried about anything specific. I'm just... on edge, I guess. I don't really know.
Before your husband passed away, did you tend to worry a lot or feel anxious in general, or is this keyed-up, on-edge feeling something that's really new for you since his death?
I don't really know... I don't think it's new. I guess I've always been kind of... restless. I never really paid that much attention to it.
When you were younger, before your husband passed away, how much did this restlessness interfere with your daily life, your relationships, or your work?

Well... it's just... lately, my family has had to help out a lot more. With the bills and, you know, paperwork. I... I guess I let things slip. And at church, and the garden club... they've had to redo things I was supposed to handle. Or find someone else to do it. It's... it's embarrassing. I just feel like... the people I care about can't really count on me anymore.

When you're sitting down trying to focus on one task, like reading or watching TV, do you find yourself getting distracted and jumping to something else because you're anxious about something, or do you just lose interest and want to move on to the next thing?

I don't think it's because I'm anxious. I just... I try to read the senior center newsletter, or look at the choir schedule, and I start out okay. But then... maybe a few minutes later, I realize I'm just looking at the same lines over and over. I don't even know what I just read. I just can't seem to keep my mind on it.

Before your husband passed away, were you generally able to keep track of things like bills, paperwork, and your commitments to the church and garden club without much difficulty, or did you struggle with staying organized even back then?

I don't really know... I guess my husband usually handled the bills and most of the paperwork. I didn't really have to do much of that. And the church stuff... I don't remember it being this hard before, but... I don't know. Maybe I just didn't notice.
When you were in school, did your teachers or parents ever say you had trouble paying attention or sitting still, or did you do okay back then?

Well... yes, I suppose so. Um... my teachers used to write on my report cards... that I was bright, but... careless. I'd lose my papers. And... they said I talked out of turn a lot. I... I guess I needed a lot of reminders to just stay in my seat and finish things. Even back in grade school.
When you were a teenager and young adult, before your husband passed away, were you still having these same troubles with staying focused and sitting still, or did things get better as you got older?

I... I don't really remember. It's been a long time since I was a teenager. I suppose I was always just... the way I am. I don't really know if it got better or worse back then. I just... I didn't really think about it much.
